assays.assay_description: Automated magnetometer HTR assay in a plastic box; mice ear-tagged with small magnets, head twitches detected by induced current. Total HTR counts recorded for 10 min (dose-response for MDMA, methylone, MBDB, psilocybin, 2C-B) or 15 min (reboxetine, atipamezole, guanfacine pretreatment experiments, including LC-ablated DBH-Cre mice).

application_type.evidence: Drugs were administered intraperitoneally (i.p.; 0.01 mL/kg) using insulin syringes.

setup_habituation.evidence: Mice were ear tagged 3 days before HTR testing; no habituation to the HTR box is described.

setup_restrain.evidence: a mouse is ear-tagged with a magnet and rapid head movements lead to induction of electric current in a wire surrounding an experimental box.

food_restriction.evidence: HTR recordings occurred in plastic boxes cleaned between recordings; no food in the apparatus.

water_restriction.evidence: No water source is described in the HTR plastic box.

time_to_assay.evidence: For HTR dose-response experiments, drugs were given immediately before testing.

outcomes.summary: Psilocybin and 2C-B dose-dependently increased HTR counts (psilocybin peaking at 3 mg/kg), whereas the entactogens MDMA and methylone suppressed HTR and MBDB produced only a small increase at 5 mg/kg. NET blockade with reboxetine unmasked MDMA-evoked HTR (greater potentiation in females) and reduced psilocybin-evoked HTR; α2R antagonism (atipamezole) enhanced MDMA HTR (females), while α2R agonism (guanfacine) suppressed both MDMA- and psilocybin-evoked HTR, including in LC-ablated mice.
outcomes.statistics: MDMA: F(4,29)=7.715, P=0.0002; methylone: Kruskal-Wallis=31.49, P<0.0001; MBDB: F(4,34)=5.010, P=0.0028; psilocybin: F(4,21)=18.00, P<0.0001; 2C-B: F(4,34)=58.59, P<0.0001; peak comparison F(5,39)=110.4, P<0.0001; reboxetine+MDMA treatment F(3,48)=5.572, P=0.0023, male vs female reboxetine+MDMA P=0.0054; reboxetine/psilocybin interaction F(1,37)=4.792, P=0.0350; atipamezole/MDMA interaction F(3,31)=6.639, P=0.0014; guanfacine/psilocybin interaction F(1,48)=14.39, P=0.0004; LC ablation treatment F(1,25)=16.34, P=0.0004
outcomes.evidence: psilocybin produced a pronounced increase in HTR beginning at 0.3 mg/kg and peaking at 3 mg/kg (Fig. 1F), while 2C-B elicited high HTR counts across a broad dose range; Mice receiving reboxetine + MDMA exhibited significantly higher HTR counts compared to animals treated with MDMA alone.

B4_ethological.evidence: HTR is explicitly excluded from ethological behaviours by the rubric; only head twitches were measured.

B5_social.evidence: Single mouse in an experimental box; no social component.

B6_cognitive.evidence: HTR is a drug-evoked reflexive head movement requiring no learning.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Automated magnetometer system with MATLAB code detects induced current from head movements — not pose estimation or ML behavioural classification.

B8_multivariate.evidence: Analyses were one-way/two-way ANOVAs on HTR counts; no dimensionality reduction.

E5_enrichment.evidence: No enrichment objects described in the HTR box.

E8_food_water.evidence: No food or water in the HTR box.

D2_session_duration.evidence: HTR assay using the same injections as B, recorded for 15 min.

assays.assay_description: Med Associates chambers: Day 1 conditioning in context A (tone co-terminating with 1 mA foot shock), Day 2 extinction training in context B (six or eight 30-s tones) with MDMA ± atipamezole, psilocybin ± guanfacine, 2C-B, methylone or MBDB given before the session, and extinction recall on Days 3 (and 4-5 for MDMA). Freezing (cue, pre-cue, inter-tone) quantified with VideoFreeze and locomotion as total distance traveled.

application_type.evidence: Drugs were administered intraperitoneally (i.p.; 0.01 mL/kg) using insulin syringes.

setup_habituation.evidence: No pre-test exposure to the conditioning chambers is described.

setup_restrain.evidence: Mice moved freely in the Med Associates chamber; freezing defined as immobility >1 s and locomotion as total distance traveled.

food_restriction.evidence: No food is present in the fear-conditioning chamber during sessions.

water_restriction.evidence: No water is present in the fear-conditioning chamber during sessions.

time_to_assay.evidence: In fear conditioning, MDMA (7.8 mg/kg) and guanfacine (0.15 mg/kg) were administered 30 min before testing, whereas psilocybin was given at trial onset.

sample_size.evidence: Group sizes for the fear conditioning experiments are reported only in Supplementary Figs. 8-12, which are not available in the main text.

outcomes.summary: MDMA given before extinction training reduced cue-elicited freezing during the earliest recall session (Day 3), an effect prevented by α2R antagonist atipamezole; by Day 5 no treatment effects remained. Psilocybin (alone or with guanfacine) did not alter freezing or locomotion, while 2C-B, methylone and MBDB produced some acute treatment effects on freezing and (methylone/MBDB) increased locomotion during training only.
outcomes.statistics: Statistics reported in Supplementary Figs. 8-12; main text notes a significant MDMA × atipamezole interaction on Day 4 (post hoc comparisons not significant) and maintained in the overall across-day analysis.
outcomes.evidence: MDMA reduced cue-elicited freezing during the earliest recall session (Day 3), but this effect was not observed when mice were pretreated with atipamezole... Psilocybin, alone or combined with guanfacine, did not significantly affect freezing or locomotor activity during extinction training on Day 2 or extinction recall on Day 3.

B1_num_measures.evidence: Freezing was quantified with VideoFreeze ... freezing was defined as immobility >1 s, and locomotion as total distance traveled; pre-cue and inter-tone freezing were also analysed.

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Freezing is compared across days and between pre-cue/cue epochs, not analysed as a within-session time course.

B3_sequential_structure.evidence: No transition or sequence analysis reported.

B4_ethological.evidence: Conditioned freezing and locomotor distance are explicitly non-ethological measures per the rubric.

B5_social.evidence: Mice were tested individually in the conditioning chamber; no social construct.

B6_cognitive.evidence: On Day 1, mice underwent fear conditioning ... underwent extinction training ... Days 3-5 extinction recall sessions.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Freezing was quantified with VideoFreeze and validated against blinded manual scoring — a motion/immobility threshold system, not a pose-estimation or ML classifier.

B8_multivariate.evidence: Two-way ANOVAs on freezing; no dimensionality reduction or multivariate analysis.

E1_environment_type.evidence: mice underwent fear conditioning (Med Associates chamber) in context A (opaque white wall, eucalyptus scent).

E2_shelter.evidence: Definitionally absent; no refuge in the conditioning chamber.

E3_bedding.evidence: Shock grid floor; chambers cleaned with 70% ethanol/Formula 409 — no bedding described.

E4_nesting.evidence: No nesting material in the conditioning chamber.

E5_enrichment.evidence: No enrichment objects in the conditioning chamber.

E6_spatial.evidence: Context A/B are single-compartment chambers differing in wall and scent cues.

E7_social_context.evidence: Mice were tested individually in the chamber.

E8_food_water.evidence: No food or water in the conditioning chamber.

D1_continuity.evidence: On Day 1, mice underwent fear conditioning ... On Day 2 ... extinction training ... Days 3-5 extinction recall sessions were identical to Day 2.

D2_session_duration.evidence: After 120 s, eight 30 s tones were presented with 45-75 s intertrial intervals, and the session ended 120 s after the last tone (~15 min).

D3_recording_days.evidence: Recording on Days 1-5 (MDMA experiment); Days 1-3 for psilocybin and other entactogens.

D4_baseline.evidence: Day 1 conditioning occurred before drug, but no pre-drug freezing baseline data is reported in the main text.

D5_followup.evidence: Days 3-5 extinction recall sessions were identical to Day 2 — i.e., ≥24 h after drug administration on Day 2.

assays.assay_description: Two-bottle choice (1% sucrose vs water) in the home cage of singly-housed mice; 14-h dark-phase sessions at baseline (Days 2-3), post-stress (Days 17-19) and 4 h after psilocybin ± guanfacine treatment (Day 20). Preference computed from bottle weights.

application_type.evidence: Drugs were administered intraperitoneally (i.p.; 0.01 mL/kg); Treatments administered on Day 20.

setup_habituation.evidence: On Day 1, mice were singly housed and habituated overnight to a two-bottle choice setup with 1.5% sucrose and water.

setup_restrain.evidence: Four hours after the final injection, mice remained in their home cages and were exposed to a 14 h overnight sucrose preference test.

food_restriction.evidence: Animals were ... provided ad libitum chow and water; testing occurred in the home cage.

water_restriction.evidence: Two-bottle choice setup with 1% sucrose and water available during the session.

time_to_assay.evidence: Four hours after the final injection, mice remained in their home cages and were exposed to a 14 h overnight sucrose preference test using a 1% sucrose solution.

sample_size.evidence: Saline + saline: N = 20; saline + psilocybin: N = 19; guanfacine + psilocybin: N = 20.

outcomes.summary: Chronic multimodal stress significantly reduced sucrose preference relative to baseline. Psilocybin-treated mice showed a modest increase in sucrose preference relative to their own stressed baseline, but post-treatment preference did not differ from saline controls; guanfacine co-treatment did not modify the outcome.
outcomes.statistics: time × treatment F(3.566, 99.86)=0.3521, P=0.8210; time F(1.783, 99.86)=39.84, P<0.0001; treatment F(2,56)=0.6856, P=0.5080; subject F(56,112)=1.990, P=0.0010; Tukey: Vehicle stress vs post-treatment P=0.9471; Psilocybin stress vs post-treatment P=0.0284; Psilocybin+Guanfacine P=0.3017; Vehicle vs Psilocybin post-treatment P=0.4606
outcomes.evidence: Although psilocybin-treated mice showed a modest numerical increase in sucrose preference following CMMS, this effect was significant only relative to their own stressed baseline and did not translate into significant differences from saline controls at the post-treatment time point.

B1_num_measures.evidence: Sucrose preference was calculated as [sucrose intake / (sucrose + water intake)] × 100.

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: Bottles were weighed before and after each session; total intake only, no within-session time course.

B3_sequential_structure.evidence: No bout or sequence analysis of licking/drinking.

B4_ethological.evidence: Only a consummatory preference ratio was computed; no natural behaviours scored as discrete acts.

B5_social.evidence: Singly housed mice tested alone; no social construct.

B6_cognitive.evidence: Sucrose preference reflects innate hedonic preference, not learning or memory.

B7_automated_classification.evidence: intake measured by weight — no automated behavioural classification.

B8_multivariate.evidence: Repeated-measures two-way ANOVA only; no multivariate analysis.

E1_environment_type.evidence: Four hours after the final injection, mice remained in their home cages and were exposed to a 14 h overnight sucrose preference test.

E2_shelter.evidence: No shelter/refuge in the home cage is described.

E3_bedding.evidence: Home-cage bedding is not described in the methods.

E5_enrichment.evidence: No enrichment objects described in the home cage.

E6_spatial.evidence: Standard home cage with two drinking bottles; no physically separated compartments.

E7_social_context.evidence: On Day 1, mice were singly housed and habituated overnight to a two-bottle choice setup.

E8_food_water.evidence: Two-bottle choice setup with 1% sucrose and water in the home cage; ad libitum chow.

D1_continuity.evidence: Baseline sucrose preference was assessed on Days 2-3 ... On Days 18-19, sucrose preference was reassessed ... post-treatment SPT on Day 20.

D2_session_duration.evidence: a 14 h overnight sucrose preference test using a 1% sucrose solution.

D3_recording_days.evidence: SPT data collected on Days 2-3 (baseline), Days 17-19 (stress) and Day 20 (post-treatment).

D4_baseline.evidence: Baseline sucrose preference was assessed on Days 2-3 using 1% sucrose during 14 h dark-phase sessions, before any drug treatment.

D5_followup.evidence: Post-treatment SPT began four hours after the final injection, not ≥24 h.

assays.assay_description: Day 21 of the CMMS protocol, 24 h after a single psilocybin ± guanfacine treatment: mice placed in a 20 cm diameter glass cylinder with 21 ± 1 °C water (15 cm depth) for 6 min; immobility scored manually during minutes 2-6 from video.

application_type.evidence: Drugs were administered intraperitoneally (i.p.; 0.01 mL/kg); Treatments administered on Day 20.

setup_habituation.evidence: No pre-exposure to the swim cylinder is described.

setup_restrain.evidence: Each mouse was placed in a 20 cm diameter glass cylinder filled with 21 ± 1 °C water (15 cm depth) for 6 min (FST cylinder counts as restraint per rubric).

food_restriction.evidence: No food is accessible in the swim cylinder.

water_restriction.evidence: Water is the test medium, not accessible drinking water.

time_to_assay.evidence: Treatments were administered on Day 20, and the FST was conducted on Day 21, approximately 24 h after a single dose.

sample_size.evidence: Saline + saline: N = 20; saline + psilocybin: N = 19; guanfacine + psilocybin: N = 20.

outcomes.summary: Psilocybin (1 mg/kg), given 24 h earlier, significantly reduced immobility in the FST relative to saline controls in chronically stressed mice, and this reduction was preserved when the α2R agonist guanfacine was co-administered.
outcomes.statistics: FST immobility on Day 21 using one-way ANOVA: F(2,56)=6.338, P=0.0033; Dunnett's post-hoc vs saline: saline+psilocybin P=0.0039; guanfacine+psilocybin P=0.0107
outcomes.evidence: psilocybin significantly reduced immobility in the FST compared with saline controls (Fig. 5C), and this reduction was preserved in the presence of guanfacine.

B1_num_measures.evidence: Immobility, defined as floating with minimal movement to keep the head above water, was scored manually during minutes 2-6.

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: A single immobility total over minutes 2-6 was reported; no within-session binning.

B3_sequential_structure.evidence: No bout or transition analysis reported.

B4_ethological.evidence: FST immobility is explicitly listed as non-ethological in the rubric.

B5_social.evidence: Each mouse was tested alone in the cylinder.

B6_cognitive.evidence: FST does not require learning or memory.

E1_environment_type.evidence: Each mouse was placed in a 20 cm diameter glass cylinder filled with 21 ± 1 °C water.

E2_shelter.evidence: Definitionally absent; no refuge in the swim cylinder.

E3_bedding.evidence: Definitionally absent; cylinder contains water only.

E6_spatial.evidence: A single cylinder with no compartments.

E7_social_context.evidence: Each mouse was placed in a ... cylinder ... for 6 min (tested individually).

E8_food_water.evidence: No food or drinking water accessible; water is the test medium.

D1_continuity.evidence: On Day 21 of the CMMS protocol (24 h after treatment), mice underwent the forced swim test.

D2_session_duration.evidence: Each mouse was placed in a ... glass cylinder ... for 6 min.

D4_baseline.evidence: No pre-drug FST session was recorded (TST, not FST, was used for pre-treatment balancing).

D5_followup.evidence: the FST was conducted on Day 21, approximately 24 h after a single dose.

judge_notes: Dropped the Tail Suspension Test assay proposed by one candidate: the TST was run on Day 19, 'the day after the final stress session', BEFORE any psychedelic treatment (treatments were administered on Day 20), and was used only to balance groups. No psychedelic was administered prior to the TST recording, so it fails the rubric's inclusion criterion (the separate Supplementary Fig. 14 TST cohort received guanfacine alone, which is not a psychedelic).

Merged all HTR variants (dose-response for five compounds, reboxetine/atipamezole/guanfacine pretreatment, LC-ablated DBH-Cre vs control) into a single Head Twitch Response assay per the rubric's 'one paradigm, many manipulations' rule.

Merged conditioning, extinction training and extinction recall (Days 1-5), across MDMA/atipamezole, psilocybin/guanfacine, 2C-B, methylone and MBDB arms, into one Fear Conditioning and Extinction assay.
Excluded fiber photometry (GRAB-NE / GRAB-5HT) recordings, histology/TH+ cell counting, and LC ablation surgery as non-behavioural.
HTR D2 set to 1 (15-60 min): the manipulation experiments state 'HTR recorded for 15 min', which falls in the 15-60 min inclusive bin; overrode the candidate that scored 0.
HTR B1 set to 0 ('1 measure' = 0 points): only total HTR counts were reported; one candidate mis-mapped the category to 1 point.
SPT D2 set to 3 (>6 h) for the 14 h overnight session; one candidate mis-binned 14 h as 61 min-6 h.
Fear conditioning D3 set to 1 point (2-7 days, Days 1-5); one candidate assigned 2 points to the '2-7' category in error.
Fear conditioning D4 scored 0: Day 1 conditioning is drug-free but the main text does not report conditioning-day freezing data as a pre-drug baseline for this assay.
Added reboxetine, atipamezole and guanfacine as dosing entries (all three were administered systemically in behavioural experiments); all candidates had omitted them.
